problem_type: stale desktop package hides protected catalog write failure
symptom: Clicking '开启 Codex 本地生图' in the installed Nomi app appears to do nothing and codex-local remains disabled.
direct_cause: The installed app is catalog schema v10 while the user's persisted model-catalog.json is schema v11. The catalog writer correctly refuses to write when the on-disk version is newer than the app version, but CodexLocalImageCard had no catch path, so the synchronous IPC exception escaped the click handler without user feedback.
class_root: Version-protected persistence failures are not represented as an actionable UI state at the shared settings control boundary; a deliberate fail-closed write can therefore look like a dead control.
affected_population: Users who open a newer Nomi catalog with an older installed desktop package
Any onboarding control that writes the model catalog while the catalog writer rejects a newer on-disk schema
Future catalog migrations if a renderer control omits its write-failure feedback path
entry_points: Model settings → Codex 本地生图 → 开启 Codex 本地生图
Catalog write protection when on-disk schema exceeds the running app schema
internal_only_reason: The version-skew guard and its user-facing recovery message are Nomi's local persistence contract; no external provider controls this behavior.
invariants: An app must never overwrite a catalog whose schema version is newer than the app understands.
A rejected catalog write must produce visible error feedback at the initiating settings control.
A successful Codex toggle must persist vendor.enabled and be observable through the same catalog read path.
The Codex local image toggle remains independent from Codex MCP assistant onboarding.
generality_proof: The writer's version guard (electron/catalog/catalogStore.ts writeCatalog, pre-existing) is shared by all catalog mutations. The renderer card now handles the same synchronous write-failure class explicitly, aligned with ComfyuiLocalCard which already caught it; codexDirectionSeparation.test.ts asserts the catch/error-toast boundary at the source level.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Translate the catalog write result or failure into visible onboarding feedback. (The fail-closed guard it reacts to, electron/catalog/catalogStore.ts writeCatalog, is pre-existing and unchanged.)

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The existing card already catches synchronous catalog writes and shows an error toast; the Codex card is aligned to that boundary.
The toggle now catches the IPC write failure and reports the original protected-write message.

recurrence.reason: Catalog schema upgrades are a normal release event and any older package can encounter a newer user catalog; every synchronous catalog control is exposed to the same protected-write failure class.
same_class_scan: Inspected all onboarding model-catalog upsertVendor callers and compared their error handling.
Inspected catalogStore.writeCatalog and CURRENT_CATALOG_VERSION against the installed app's extracted catalogStore/types bundle.
Read the real user catalog and confirmed version 11; extracted /Applications/Nomi.app and confirmed its compiled CURRENT_CATALOG_VERSION is 10.
Compared the Codex card toggle against ComfyuiLocalCard's enable/disable handlers, which already catch the synchronous catalog write and toast the failure.

prevention.invariant: Newer persisted catalog schemas remain read-only, and every initiating settings control must surface the rejected-write reason.
prevention.failure_mode: The write is refused without data loss; the user sees the explicit version-protection error instead of a silent no-op.
prevention.strategy: Keep the fail-closed persistence guard (catalogStore.writeCatalog) and add the missing renderer error path at the Codex settings control; codexDirectionSeparation.test.ts asserts the catch/error-toast at source.

legacy_paths.rationale: The fail-closed version guard is retained; the missing error feedback path is added without creating a parallel persistence implementation.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: This is an internal Electron persistence and renderer feedback contract.

migration: No data migration is performed by the toggle. Users on an older package must update to a build that understands the persisted catalog schema; bypassing the guard would risk dropping newer fields.
residual_risks: The currently installed /Applications/Nomi.app remains an older package until a newer build is installed; source changes alone cannot alter that already-built binary.
The source-level test proves the catch/error-toast exists; a stale package's failure toast can only be observed at runtime after installing the patched build.
